newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Clinton nuke has earthquake alert.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Clinton nuke has earthquake alert.

text.p: Illinois Power Co's 930 megawatt Clinton nuclear power plant experienced an unusual event Monday night when seismic monitoring devices detected a possible earthquake in the area, a spokesman said Tuesday.
"At about 10:10 (2210 CST/2310 EST) on Monday we had some of Clinton's monitoring devices go off," spokesman John Dewey said.
The plant, located in Clinton, Ill., was already shut for a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage at the time of the seismic alert.
Officials found no evidence of damage to the plant during inspections early Tuesday, Dewey said, adding there have been no outside confirmations of any seismic activity in the area.
"We have had no confirmation of any seismic activity. We are evaluating right now what set off these sensitive seismic devices," the spokesman said.
The seismic alert was expected to have no effect on the length of the plant's outage.
The Clinton plant was shut Sept 5 to correct a recirculation pump problem. The outage was extended to address safety issues and to refuel the plant.
Dewey said no restart date has yet been set for the plant.
Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily plant status report Tuesday that the plant is tentatively scheduled to restart Feb 11.
But Dewey discounted the NRC date, again saying no restart has been set for the plant.
